payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of RAG1-p.Arg404Gln (RAG1, UniProt P15918) and test it with one targeted computational test.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_000448.3(RAG1):c.1211G>A (p.Arg404Gln) as Pathogenic (reviewed by expert panel; 3 of 4 stars; 12 submissions) for RAG1 deficiency.
payload.strength: reviewed by expert panel (3 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: AlphaMissense gives p.Arg404Gln of P15918 a pathogenicity of 0.9531, classed as likely pathogenic (scale 0 to 1).
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use

payload.statement: ScoreCons gives residue 404 of P15918 a conservation score of 1.0 (UniRef90; 0 to 1, higher = more conserved).
EVE gives p.Arg404Gln of P15918 a score of 0.673, classed as pathogenic (scale 0 to 1).
UniProtKB annotates residues 392-459 of P15918 as the DNA binding region NBD, and InterPro annotates residues 390-460 as the RAG nonamer-binding domain; residue 404 lies inside both.
payload.strength: UniProtKB ECO:0000255 (rank 1 of 3); InterPro domain match, not graded

payload.statement: Zero of the experimental PDB structures of P15918 observe residue 404; the only structure covering the full sequence is the predicted AlphaFold DB model AF-P15918-F1 with mean pLDDT 81.56.
payload.strength: PDBe SIFTS residue-level mapping; AlphaFold model pLDDT 81.56

payload.statement: ClinVar lists p.Arg404Trp at the same residue as Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic with 2 of 4 review stars, so two different substitutions at residue 404 are both disease-associated.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: UniProtKB states RAG1 is the catalytic component of the RAG complex mediating DNA cleavage in V(D)J recombination, with RAG1 mediating DNA binding, and that it forms a homodimer and a RAG1-RAG2 complex.
A systematic analysis of recombination activity and genotype-phenotype correlation in human RAG1 deficiency has been published in J Allergy Clin Immunol (2014).
Europe PMC returned no publication that names the R404Q variant in its title or abstract for this search; the four hits are general RAG1 papers.
payload.strength: search result, 4 general hits, none naming R404Q in abstract

payload.statement: No experimental structure observes residue 404 of RAG1, and no functional assay covers the residue; whether R404 contacts DNA, the partner protein or the fold is not known from the record.
payload.why_it_matters: Without a contact or assay, the three mechanism classes (DNA binding, folding, dimer/partner contact) cannot be separated from the starting evidence.

payload.statement: No publication retrieved in this run measures recombination activity, DNA binding or protein folding of p.Arg404Gln specifically.
payload.why_it_matters: The pathogenic label rests on ClinVar and in-silico scores, so the molecular cause is still untested.

payload.statement: The Arg404 side chain in the RAG1 nonamer-binding domain makes a positively charged contact with the RSS DNA backbone; Gln removes that charge and reduces DNA binding, so recombination activity falls.
payload.would_refute: A DNA-binding or electrophoretic mobility assay with R404Q RAG1 showing binding equal to wild type, or residue 404 lying outside any DNA-contacting surface in a structure.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Residue sits in the annotated DNA-binding NBD (E5), is fully conserved (E3), and both disease substitutions at this residue are pathogenic (E1, E7), so a DNA-contact loss is the most direct reading of the annotation.

payload.statement: The Arg404Gln substitution destabilises the folded nonamer-binding domain, lowering the amount of properly folded RAG1 and so reducing recombination activity.
payload.would_refute: A computed stability change near zero for R404Q on the AlphaFold model, with the residue solvent-exposed and not packing, and no loss of folding in an expression or stability assay.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Conservation and the AlphaMissense and EVE scores are high (E2, E3, E4), which fits a fold-level cost, but the model has only moderate confidence (pLDDT 81.56, E6) and no experimental structure exists to confirm a packing role.

payload.statement: Arg404 forms part of the RAG1 homodimer or RAG1-RAG2 interface; Gln breaks that contact so the active complex does not assemble.
payload.would_refute: A structural-context or interface analysis showing residue 404 is buried away from the dimer interface and an intact assembly for R404Q in a binding assay.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: RAG1 is annotated as a homodimer in a complex with RAG2 (E8), but the record gives no interface residues, so this is the least supported of the three.

payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Clear destabilising result would move H2 to rank 1; neutral result would weaken H2 and leave H1 (DNA contact, which a fold assay cannot see) as the open favourite.

## Question
What molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of RAG1 p.Arg404Gln (UniProt P15918), and which single computational test checks it? [E1]

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies RAG1 p.Arg404Gln as Pathogenic, reviewed by an expert panel [E1]. The other substitution at the same residue, p.Arg404Trp, is also Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic [E7]. Residue 404 lies inside the UniProt DNA-binding NBD (392–459) and the InterPro nonamer-binding domain (390–460) [E5]. ScoreCons conservation is 1.0 [E3]. AlphaMissense gives 0.9531 and EVE gives 0.673, both in the pathogenic class [E2, E4]. No experimental structure observes residue 404 [E6]. No retrieved paper measures R404Q activity or binding [G2, E10].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (nucleic acid binding, ranked first): the Arg404 side chain contacts the RSS DNA backbone, and Gln removes that contact [H1, E5]. H2 (stability): the substitution destabilises the NBD fold [H2, E2, E3]. H3 (protein interaction): residue 404 sits in the RAG1 homodimer or RAG2 interface [H3, E8]. Each has a refutation criterion recorded [H1, H2, H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
Three candidates were recorded [T1, T2, T3]. T3, a ligand-contact test, cannot run because no experimental structure covers the residue [T3]. T1, a FoldX stability test, was chosen because it runs now at no compute cost, needs no approval, and bears directly on H2 [T1]. T2, a pocket and interface test, was the alternative for H3 [T2].

## Result
FoldX predicts a folding free-energy change of -0.79 kcal/mol for R404Q on the AlphaFold model, at residue pLDDT 93.56 [T1]. The 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold was not reached [T1]. R404W at the same residue gives -0.79 kcal/mol [T1].

## Updated decision
H2 is weakened by the small predicted fold cost [T1]. H1 remains favoured, as it was before the test [H1]. T1 does not measure DNA contact, so H1 is still untested [T1].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
FoldX on a predicted model has errors near 1 kcal/mol, so a neutral value does not show that R404Q is tolerated [T1]. No experimental structure confirms the model at this residue [E6]. DNA binding, interface contact and recombination activity of R404Q were not measured, so all three hypotheses remain open [G1, G2].

## Next experiment
Run the structural context test T2 to test H3 [T2]. Then measure whether R404 contacts the RSS backbone in a DNA-bound RAG1 model or structure, to test H1 [H1]. A contact under about 4 Å would support H1; no contact would overturn it.
